From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 8:14 AM PST
Subject: Exec update: ABM pilot midpoint (regulated workloads) — pipeline + risks + asks

Team — midpoint readout on the 6–8 week regulated workloads ABM pilot (FinServ + Healthcare). Keeping this tight; details in the attached snapshot.

Where we are (as of EOD 2/11)

1) Top-of-funnel + meetings
- Target accounts: 68 (FinServ 38 / Healthcare 30)
- Meetings booked: 11 total (FinServ 7 / Healthcare 4)
- “Security-first” CTA is working: 6 of 11 were booked off “30-min security review + reference architecture walkthrough” vs a generic product demo

2) Pipeline + stage progress (early, but real)
- Net-new pipeline created (Dedicated/Private qualified): ~$1.3M (weighted ~$420k)
- 3 accounts in active evaluation planning (POC scoped or being scoped)
  - 2 FinServ (VPC Private strongly preferred)
  - 1 Healthcare (on-prem interest; unclear if realistic in pilot window)
- 2 accounts have initiated formal security questionnaires / evidence requests (good signal; also time-consuming)

3) What’s resonating (messaging)
- FinServ: “predictable latency + auditability + isolation without building a serving platform”
- Healthcare: “PHI constraints + deployment boundaries + retention controls” BUT we’re hitting more procurement/legal gates (BAA/DPA questions earlier)

4) What’s slowing us down (risks)
A) Security review cycle time
- We’re still seeing inconsistent answers in email threads when questions move from AE → SE → Security.
- The approved retention/residency language is helping, but we need a single “questionnaire-ready” bundle that’s easy to reuse.

B) Private deployment clarity
- Prospects keep asking for: exact audit log export formats, KMS/HSM integration specifics, and an “operational responsibility matrix” (Redwood vs customer).
- If we can’t answer crisply in one doc + one diagram, the technical deep dives drift.

C) On-prem expectations (Healthcare)
- We need to be careful not to “sell” on-prem as if it’s drop-in. Current conversations are manageable if we frame on-prem as: “possible via Private package, subject to discovery + readiness assessment.”

Asks / decisions for the next 2 weeks

1) Resourcing to reduce security friction (highest leverage)
- Request: 1 named Security Eng (Marcus) + 1 named GRC (Olga) office-hours slot 2x/week for ABM (45 min each), plus a single source-of-truth FAQ addendum per vertical.
- Goal: cut time-to-first-security-response from ~4–5 business days to <48 hours.

2) Product/Eng clarity on Private claims (to avoid over-promise)
- Request: Vivek/Naomi to confirm what we can state as GA vs beta for:
  - Audit log export (supported destinations/formats)
  - KMS integration boundaries (customer-managed keys vs bring-your-own)
  - Private control plane RBAC/SSO posture
- If we can’t lock this down, we should tighten copy and adjust outbound accordingly.

3) Pilot scale decision (end of week 6)
- Decision we’ll need: do we (a) double down on FinServ only for repeatability, or (b) keep both verticals and invest in healthcare legal/security packaging (BAA/DPA language, retention defaults, etc.).
- My current view: FinServ is closer to repeatable motion; Healthcare is higher friction unless we invest in “packaged proof.”

4) Commercial guardrails for evaluations
- Request: pre-approval to offer up to $25k in usage credits per qualified Private eval (strict criteria + MAP) without CRO escalation each time.
- Rationale: we’re losing momentum while we wait for exception approvals.

Attachments:
- ABM_Pilot_Midpoint_Snapshot_2026-02-12.pdf
- ABM_Pilot_Account_Status_2026-02-12.csv
- Regulated_Workloads_Messaging_Guardrails_v0.9.docx

If you reply, please focus on the asks above + any red flags you want us to handle before we scale.

Jordan
—
Jordan Blake
CRO, Redwood Inference


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Exec update: ABM pilot midpoint (regulated workloads) — pipeline + risks + asks

Agree on highest leverage being cycle time + consistency.

Two red flags to manage tightly:
1) Retention language drift. I’ve already seen “we don’t store prompts/outputs” show up in a draft response. That’s not an approved blanket statement across deployment modes. We can say what is true today and what controls exist (and when storage is customer-managed), but we have to keep it precise.

2) “On-prem” phrasing. If we imply a general availability on-prem installer without a readiness assessment + support boundaries, we’ll set ourselves up for a trust gap.

I support office hours. Proposal:
- Marcus Lin + Olga Petrov: Tues/Thurs 1:00–1:45pm PT (starting next week)
- Kevin Osei can also join the first 2 sessions to ensure we’re aligning with the FAQ addenda.

On the GA vs beta clarification: Naomi and I can provide a one-pager with the allowed statements + evidence we can share (under NDA vs not) by Monday EOD.

Aisha


From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:34 AM PST
Subject: Re: Exec update: ABM pilot midpoint (regulated workloads) — pipeline + risks + asks

+1 to tightening claims. We can make the campaign repeatable if we treat “security bundle” as a product.

Marketing asks / actions on our side:
- If Aisha/Naomi deliver the allowed-claims one-pager Monday, Soojin + Ethan can refactor the landing page copy and the outbound templates by Wednesday.
- We need a single “request access” flow for evidence packages (SOC2 report, pen test summary, etc.) with clear NDA gating. Right now we’re doing it ad hoc in email.

On scale decision: I’m aligned with focusing on FinServ for repeatability, unless we explicitly resource healthcare legal/compliance packaging. “Keep both” without adding capacity will dilute.

Jordan — on the $25k credits pre-approval: from a marketing spend POV I’m supportive as long as Sales Ops defines strict qualification and we track it (MAP required, target tier 1/2 only).

Camila


From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Exec update: ABM pilot midpoint (regulated workloads) — pipeline + risks + asks

Adding field perspective from SE:

What’s blocking technical progression is not performance — it’s crisp answers on boundaries.

Top 5 repeat questions we need to answer in one place:
1) VPC networking: peering options, DNS/TLS assumptions, ingress/egress expectations
2) Audit logging: what events, how to export, and what’s “customer operated” vs “Redwood operated”
3) Key management: where KMS integrates, and what we do/don’t ever access
4) Data handling defaults per deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private (and who stores what)
5) RACI: who owns patching, monitoring, incident response, and access control

If we can ship a “Private/VPC reference architecture + ops responsibility matrix” that’s stable, we can reuse it on every deep dive and shorten calls.

I can spare Simran Kaur for 3–4 hours early next week to align the diagram + RACI with Security wording, but we need a decision owner to approve the final artifact (Vivek/Naomi?).

Markus


From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>, Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Isabelle Laurent <isabelle.laurent@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 12:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Exec update: ABM pilot midpoint (regulated workloads) — pipeline + risks + asks

Thanks all. Locking next steps:

1) Security office hours
- Confirmed: Tues/Thurs 1:00–1:45pm PT starting next week (Marcus + Olga + Kevin for first 2).
- Aisha/Naomi to send the “allowed statements + evidence sharing rules” one-pager by Monday EOD.

2) Private/VPC “single bundle” artifact
- Markus: please have Simran draft the ops responsibility matrix (RACI) + update the reference architecture diagram.
- Vivek/Naomi: please be final approvers on the artifact (accuracy + roadmap-safe language). Target: internal final by next Friday; external shareable version after Security sign-off.

3) Evidence access flow
- Camila/Tyler (looping offline): create a single intake + NDA gating process for evidence package requests. Goal: no more custom hunting in email.

4) Credits pre-approval
- I’m comfortable with the $25k cap for *qualified* Private evaluations, but only with:
  - Tier 1/2 target accounts
  - MAP completed with 2–3 week technical plan + named decision criteria
  - Sales Ops tracking (Isabelle — can you define the HubSpot fields + a simple approval checkbox?)

5) Scale decision
- We’ll make the call at end of week 6 with data. For now: keep both verticals running, but bias rep/SE time toward FinServ unless healthcare shows a faster path through legal/security.

If anything above is a blocker, raise it today — otherwise I’m treating as go.

Jordan
—
Jordan Blake
CRO, Redwood Inference
